items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The youngest uncle referred to just now was Uncle Nat.

ctx.x: Okay. We can move on. What I’m curious about at this point is the moment in time when the family is deciding to move North, what prompts that decision, and to what extent you as a five-year-old might be aware of what energies are going on, because you’re getting ready to start this journey.

Let me say this. There was not – there was only two people – that was my father and my youngest uncle – came up to Chicago first and established – came there to work. Then the family – other parts of the family moved up to Chicago. That’s when my aunt and my mother – but my father and my uncle went first. My father went into the stockyards. They both did. They both went into the stockyards. The youngest uncle referred to just now was Uncle Nat.
